His chest tightened. Do something, his mind screamed.
Then he remembered what his therapist had said:
“Urges are like waves. You don’t have to fight them. You just have to ride them.”
Ride them? he had laughed back then. But now, standing there, he had nothing to lose.
He took a slow breath. He didn’t pick up the phone. He didn’t distract himself either. He just… noticed.
The tightness in his chest.
The restlessness in his hands.
The thoughts whispering, Just this once.
He imagined the urge as a wave rising in front of him. Tall, powerful… but not permanent.
He kept breathing.
The wave rose higher. For a moment, it felt unbearable—as if it would crash over him completely.
But he stayed.
And then, slowly, something strange happened.
It softened.
The tightness loosened just a little. The thoughts became quieter. The wave… started to fall.
Five minutes passed. Then ten.
He looked at his phone again. The urge was still there—but it no longer controlled him.
He smiled faintly, put the phone back in his pocket, and ordered a cup of tea.
For the first time, he realized—
he didn’t have to stop
